title: Calibration orchestration: privacy-tiered artifact retention, signed provenance, and validation gates
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Scope: Add orchestration features in Redwood Console to manage calibration runs (FP8/INT8), their artifacts, and accuracy validation results with privacy-aware, tiered retention controls and cryptographic provenance. The goal is to let orgs define retention policies per-project and per-sensitivity tier, ensure artifacts used for model quantization and calibration are signed and auditable, and gate deployment rollouts based on accuracy validation thresholds. This will enable compliance with customer data retention requirements, reduce storage costs, and improve trust in calibration artifacts for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: administrators can create per-project retention policies with tiers (short, standard, long, archival) and default TTLs
API: calibration-run artifacts created via REST/SDK contain provenance headers (run_id, model_hash, profile_hash, signer_id, signature) and are retrievable via API with integrity checks
Storage: artifacts can be encrypted at rest and signed using customer or Redwood-managed KMS keys; HSM-backed signing for customers who opt in
Retention enforcement: GC process honors per-tenant TTLs, supports soft-delete window (configurable), and leaves an immutable audit stub record after deletion
RBAC: only roles with delete_artifact permission can override TTL; all overrides are recorded in audit logs with actor and justification
Validation gating: a calibration run can produce an accuracy report; the Console can block rollout if accuracy regressions exceed configured thresholds
Telemetry: metrics emitted for artifact count, avg retention, storage bytes per-customer, and number of signed artifacts
End-to-end tests: integration test that creates a calibration run, signs artifacts, verifies retrieval + signature, applies TTL, and observes GC deletion and audit stub creation
design_decisions: Soft-delete by default to support accidental delete recovery vs immediate hard-delete for strict compliance tenants
Use asymmetric signing (ECDSA) for artifact provenance to allow public verification without exposing secret keys; offer HMAC as lower-cost option for internal teams
Per-tenant TTLs stored in metadata layer rather than encoded in object keys to support future policy changes without re-writing objects
Retention tiers (short/standard/long/archival) map to different storage classes (hot/object-store/cold) to optimize cost
Accuracy gating lives in the rollout controller (Console + Runtime) — chosen to avoid coupling artifact storage lifecycle with rollout logic while maintaining a clear signal path
tradeoffs: Immediate hard-delete reduces exposure but complicates auditability and recovery; chosen default is soft-delete with optional hard-delete for compliance tenants
HSM-backed signing increases cost and engineering effort but provides the strongest customer guarantees; offered as opt-in premium feature
Storing TTLs centrally adds a dependency on metadata service availability; mitigated with cached TTLs in runtime and periodic reconciliation
rollout_plan: Internal dogfood: enable for 3 internal teams and run synthetic calibration jobs for FP8/INT8 across multiple models
Beta: invite 5 pilot customers (mix of Hosted, Dedicated, Private); collect feedback on UI, retention defaults, and signing UX
Hardening: complete security review (SEC-411), performance tuning for GC (ENG-20745), and S3 lifecycle rules integration (ENG-20122)
GA: flip feature flag and enable by default for new projects; provide migration tooling for existing artifacts
metrics: Artifact storage delta (GB) per-week after retention enforcement
Avg time-to-delete after TTL expiry (s) and percent completed within SLO
Percentage of artifacts with valid signatures
Number of forced-deletes / TTL overrides and associated audit entries
Rollout blocks triggered by accuracy gating and false-positive rate
implementation_notes: Backend changes: metadata schema to include retention_tier, signer_id, signature_blob, model_hash, profile_hash
GC service: incremental sweeper that uses metadata index to avoid full listing; support warm/cold storage migration
API additions: POST /calibration-runs/{id}/artifacts with optional signer_kms_key param; GET artifact returns provenance headers
Console UX: retention policy editor in project settings, artifact detail panel shows provenance and signature verification status
Security: integrate with KMS + HSM providers; require security review before enabling customer-managed keys
dependencies_notes: ENG-20122: S3 lifecycle + multi-region replication improvements (blocking for archival tier)
ENG-20745: GC service performance and indexer to avoid listing millions of objects
SEC-411: security review for KMS/HSM signing and audit storage
ENG-21500: rollout controller hook for validation gating integration
